sentiment.rationale: Guidance was reaffirmed but management explicitly stated results may trend toward the lower end of the provided EPS range, indicating a downward tilt in forward expectations. The North America business underperformed expectations in Q2, and management cited headwinds from high gas prices and commodity inflation. The reaffirmation without a raise, combined with cautious language about the second half, results in a slightly negative score.

summary.revenue: Net revenue increased 6.4% in Q2 2026 to $24,181 million, and 7.3% year-to-date to $43,624 million. Organic revenue increased 2.4% in Q2 and 2.5% year-to-date.
summary.eps: Reported EPS increased 137% to $2.18 in Q2 2026, and 72% year-to-date to $3.88. Core EPS increased 4% to $2.20 in Q2, and 6% year-to-date to $3.81.
summary.guidance: Company affirms fiscal 2026 financial guidance: organic revenue to increase between 2 and 4 percent; core constant currency EPS to increase between 4 and 6 percent; core annual effective tax rate of approximately 22 percent; capital spending below 5% of net revenue; free cash flow conversion ratio of at least 80 percent; total cash returns to shareholders of approximately $8.9 billion. Management indicated results may trend toward the lower end of the EPS range.
summary.margin: Operating margin expanded 875 bps to 16.6% in Q2, primarily due to prior-year impairment charges. Core operating margin contracted 40 bps to 16.8% in Q2. Year-to-date operating margin expanded 585 bps to 16.6%; core operating margin contracted 15 bps to 16.3%.
key_risks: High fuel prices impacting convenience store traffic and conversion of store traffic into purchases.
More pressure on the business from a commodity standpoint in the second half, particularly affecting the EMEA region.
North America business softer than expected in Q2, with gradual improvement expected at a more moderate pace.
Higher tax rate year-over-year expected in Q3.
Impulse channel softness due to high fuel prices.
key_opportunities: International business expected to exceed $40 billion in revenue for the full year, with strong growth and margin expansion.
Permissible food portfolio reached $3 billion and growing at nearly double-digit rate.
Tariff refund claims expected to contribute approximately 1 percentage point to full-year EPS growth.
Record productivity levels in first half, with additional layers of cost reduction planned in second half.
Testing mixing centers in Texoma to lower transportation and delivery costs.
World Cup sponsorship helping activate categories in Europe and Latin America.
